question: How does BSP scale CET across the Northeast?
html:
Scaling CET across the Northeast

BSP scales CET as a ~3x buy-and-build over 36 months, modelled on Smith + Howard. The sequence is to integrate MA and CT around Horton's wastewater work, buy founder-owned firms in RI, NH, ME and VT, then shift the mix toward recurring service contracts that earn a higher multiple (CET growth plan).

The four-phase path

  • Phase 1: Run MA and CT as one company. Point Horton at 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects in CT, MA and RI, led by New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk (CET growth plan).
  • Phase 2: Use CET's existing six-state licensing to buy into RI, NH, ME and VT. The screen covers 48 companies with a ~$15.1M median (CET growth plan).
  • Phase 3: Add SCADA and pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency work. The aim is a mix that PKF and Capstone price 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).
  • Phase 4: Gated at month 24. The context is truncated here, so its scope needs the full growth plan.
  • Data-center electrical is real upside in PJM but thin in New England (CET growth plan).

Where demand sits

  • The opportunity count is highest in CT (27) and MA (25), then ME (16), VT (9), NH (5) and RI (4) (CET opportunity radar).
  • Funded CT pump-station programs include Fairfield at ~$36.1M est. and Danbury electrical resiliency at ~$3.2M est. (CET opportunity radar).
  • The MA state revolving fund list is not itemized because automated access was blocked (CET opportunity radar).

Gap in the target list

  • The ranked top 10 is nine MA firms and one CT firm. None is in RI, NH, ME or VT (CET add-on targets).
  • That fits Phase 1 tuck-ins but not Phase 2.
  • McDonald Electrical (~$18.4M est.) runs ANJ Electric, a RI/CT union contractor, as a division. It is a possible bridge into RI (CET add-on targets).
  • Revenues are ZoomInfo estimates. Several conflict with headcount and need diligence (CET add-on targets).

Next actions

  • Today and tomorrow: Confirm submission of the Massport Worcester airport 149A RFQ and the BPS and Campbell generator bids, all due Oct 8, 2026. Finish the SRTA New Bedford charger bid, due Oct 9, 2026 (CET opportunity radar).
  • CT wastewater: Put Horton's CT team on the River Road pump-station bid, due Oct 15, 2026. Book engineer-of-record meetings for Fairfield, South Windsor, West Haven and Danbury.
  • Target screen: Rebuild the top 10 with a separate RI/NH/ME/VT ranking. Open early contact with McDonald.
  • Baselines: Pull the MassDEP 2026 Intended Use Plan tables by hand. Replace the estimated CET baselines with actual management financials before locking month-12 targets.
